blocks.en: "He said to them, 'But who do you say that I am?'" — Matthew 16:15
blocks.es_reference: "Él les dijo: Y vosotros, ¿quién decís que soy yo?" — Mateo 16:15 (RVG)

blocks.en: The Question He Forces
blocks.es_reference: La Pregunta que Él Obliga

blocks.en: Sooner or later every road in apologetics arrives at one Person and one question. Jesus turned to His own disciples and asked it plainly: "Who do you say that I am?" It is the question He still asks every man, and He has arranged matters so that we cannot dodge it with a polite half-answer. The world would love to file Jesus away as a great moral teacher, a kind rabbi, one wise voice among many. But He will not fit in that drawer, for a great moral teacher does not say the things this Man said. He forgave sins that were not committed against Him. He accepted worship that no prophet ever dared accept. He said, "Before Abraham was, I AM," taking on His own lips the holy name of God. He told men that He and the Father were one, and that to see Him was to see the Father. A teacher of morals does not talk this way. Either these are the ravings of a deluded man, or the lies of a wicked one, or they are simply true.
blocks.es_reference: Tarde o temprano todo camino en la apologética llega a una Persona y a una pregunta. Jesús se volvió a sus propios discípulos y la hizo claramente: "¿Quién decís que soy yo?" Es la pregunta que todavía le hace a todo hombre, y ha dispuesto las cosas de modo que no podamos esquivarla con una cortés media respuesta. Al mundo le encantaría archivar a Jesús como un gran maestro de moral, un rabino amable, una voz sabia entre muchas. Pero Él no cabe en ese cajón, porque un gran maestro de moral no dice las cosas que este Hombre dijo. Perdonó pecados que no se cometieron contra Él. Aceptó adoración que ningún profeta jamás se atrevió a aceptar. Dijo: "Antes que Abraham fuese, yo soy", tomando en sus propios labios el santo nombre de Dios. Les dijo a los hombres que Él y el Padre eran uno, y que verlo a Él era ver al Padre. Un maestro de moral no habla así. O estos son los delirios de un hombre engañado, o las mentiras de uno malvado, o son sencillamente verdad.

blocks.en: Liar, Lunatic, or Lord
blocks.es_reference: Mentiroso, Lunático o Señor

blocks.en: This is the famous fork in the road. A man who said about himself what Jesus said is not left to us as a good teacher and nothing more; that one option, the comfortable one, He has closed with His own words. If His claims to deity were false and He knew they were false, then He was a liar of the blackest kind, deceiving the very people He told to trust Him. If His claims were false and He did not know it, if He sincerely believed He was God when He was not, then He was a lunatic on the level of a man who believes he is a poached egg, and no wise sayings could redeem such madness. But if His claims were true, then He is exactly who He said He is — the Lord. Liar, lunatic, or Lord: those are the doors, and the door marked "merely a fine teacher" was bricked up by Jesus Himself. The apologist's task is to press the honest man up against this fork and not let him slip past it.
blocks.es_reference: Esta es la famosa bifurcación del camino. Un hombre que dijo de sí mismo lo que Jesús dijo no nos queda como un buen maestro y nada más; esa opción, la cómoda, Él la cerró con sus propias palabras. Si sus afirmaciones de deidad eran falsas y Él lo sabía, entonces era un mentiroso de la peor clase, engañando a la gente misma a quien decía que confiara en Él. Si sus afirmaciones eran falsas y no lo sabía, si sinceramente creía que era Dios cuando no lo era, entonces era un lunático al nivel de un hombre que cree que es un huevo escalfado, y ningún dicho sabio podría redimir tal locura. Pero si sus afirmaciones eran verdaderas, entonces es exactamente quien dijo ser — el Señor. Mentiroso, lunático o Señor: esas son las puertas, y la puerta que dice "solo un buen maestro" fue tapiada por Jesús mismo. La tarea del apologista es llevar al hombre honesto hasta esta bifurcación y no dejarlo pasar de largo.

blocks.en: The Fingerprint of Prophecy
blocks.es_reference: La Huella de la Profecía

blocks.en: How shall we know which door is the true one? One great evidence is what we may call the pre-written biography. Centuries before this Man was born, the prophets sketched His portrait in advance. Micah named the village of His birth, Bethlehem, seven hundred years early. The twenty-second Psalm described a death by the piercing of hands and feet and the casting of lots for the sufferer's clothing — written a thousand years before the Romans had even invented crucifixion as a way to kill a man. Isaiah, in his fifty-third chapter, drew the suffering servant so exactly that men have called it the fifth Gospel. These are not vague horoscopes that fit anyone; they are specific, and they all converge on one life.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Cómo sabremos cuál puerta es la verdadera? Una gran evidencia es lo que podríamos llamar la biografía escrita por adelantado. Siglos antes de que este Hombre naciera, los profetas bosquejaron su retrato con anticipación. Miqueas nombró la aldea de su nacimiento, Belén, setecientos años antes. El Salmo veintidós describió una muerte por la perforación de las manos y los pies y el echar suertes sobre la ropa del que sufría — escrito mil años antes de que los romanos hubieran siquiera inventado la crucifixión como manera de matar a un hombre. Isaías, en su capítulo cincuenta y tres, dibujó al siervo sufriente con tal exactitud que algunos lo han llamado el quinto Evangelio. Estos no son horóscopos vagos que le quedan a cualquiera; son específicos, y todos convergen en una sola vida.

blocks.en: The Silver Dollars of Texas
blocks.es_reference: Los Dólares de Plata de Texas

blocks.en: The mathematician Peter Stoner, writing in a book reviewed by the American Scientific Affiliation, estimated the odds of a single man fulfilling just eight of these prophecies by chance at one in ten to the seventeenth power. That number is too large for the mind to feel, so let me give it a shape. Imagine covering the whole state of Texas with silver dollars two feet deep. Mark just one of them with red paint and stir them all together. Now blindfold a man, set him loose anywhere in the state, and tell him he may stoop just once and must come up with the marked coin on the first try. His chance is roughly the chance that one man should fulfill eight prophecies by accident. This calculation rests on assigning a probability to each prophecy individually, a method some statisticians have questioned, so it is best taken as a vivid illustration of just how improbable coincidence would be rather than an exact, uncontested figure. And Jesus is traditionally reckoned to have fulfilled not eight but several hundred more.
blocks.es_reference: El matemático Peter Stoner, en un libro revisado por la Asociación Científica Estadounidense, estimó las probabilidades de que un solo hombre cumpliera por azar solo ocho de estas profecías en una en diez elevado a la diecisiete. Ese número es demasiado grande para que la mente lo sienta, así que déjeme darle forma. Imagine cubrir todo el estado de Texas con dólares de plata, de dos pies de profundidad. Marque solo uno de ellos con pintura roja y revuélvalos todos. Ahora vende los ojos a un hombre, suéltelo en cualquier parte del estado, y dígale que puede agacharse una sola vez y debe sacar la moneda marcada en el primer intento. Su probabilidad es aproximadamente la probabilidad de que un hombre cumpla ocho profecías por accidente. Este cálculo se basa en asignar una probabilidad a cada profecía individualmente, un método que algunos estadísticos han cuestionado, así que es mejor tomarlo como una ilustración vívida de lo improbable que sería la coincidencia, no como una cifra exacta e incontrovertible. Y a Jesús tradicionalmente se le atribuye el cumplimiento no de ocho sino de varios cientos más.

blocks.en: 💡 Let me tell you a story; it never happened, but the truth it carries did. Imagine a man given a great mosaic, but given it one tile at a time, over forty years, by forty strangers who never met one another. The first hands him a fragment of blue, the next a shard of gold, the next a jagged black edge. For decades it looks like a heap of broken rubbish with no shape at all. Then the last piece is set in place, and all at once the heap resolves into a face. That is the testimony of the prophets. No single prophet saw the whole picture, but when Jesus came, He was the only person in all of history whose life fit every jagged piece of a portrait fifteen centuries in the making.
blocks.es_reference: 💡 Déjeme contarle una historia; nunca sucedió, pero la verdad que lleva sí sucedió. Imagine a un hombre a quien se le da un gran mosaico, pero se le da una pieza a la vez, durante cuarenta años, por cuarenta desconocidos que nunca se conocieron entre sí. El primero le entrega un fragmento azul, el siguiente una esquirla dorada, el siguiente un borde negro y dentado. Por décadas parece un montón de basura rota sin forma alguna. Entonces se coloca la última pieza, y de repente el montón se resuelve en un rostro. Ese es el testimonio de los profetas. Ningún profeta solo vio el cuadro entero, pero cuando Jesús vino, fue la única persona en toda la historia cuya vida encajó en cada pieza dentada de un retrato quince siglos en construcción.

blocks.en: God With Us
blocks.es_reference: Dios con Nosotros

blocks.en: Run the thread back to its beginning. Long before Bethlehem, Isaiah told a faithless king that God Himself would give a sign: "Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a Son, and shall call His name Immanuel" (Isaiah 7:14). And when the angel came to Joseph, Matthew tells us this was its fulfillment: the child would be called Immanuel, "which is translated, God with us" (Matthew 1:23). That is the heart of the whole matter. The name is not "God above us," watching from a distance, nor "God against us," armed and angry, but God with us — the Almighty come near enough to be held by a peasant girl and laid in a feeding trough. The claims and the prophecies point to the same astonishing thing: that in this Man, God Himself came down to be with His people.
blocks.es_reference: Siga el hilo hasta su comienzo. Mucho antes de Belén, Isaías le dijo a un rey sin fe que Dios mismo daría una señal: "He aquí que la virgen concebirá, y dará a luz un hijo, y llamará su nombre Emanuel" (Isaías 7:14). Y cuando el ángel vino a José, Mateo nos dice que esto era su cumplimiento: el niño sería llamado Emanuel, "que traducido es: Dios con nosotros" (Mateo 1:23). Ese es el corazón de todo el asunto. El nombre no es "Dios sobre nosotros", mirando desde lejos, ni "Dios contra nosotros", armado y airado, sino Dios con nosotros — el Todopoderoso acercándose lo bastante para ser cargado por una muchacha campesina y acostado en un comedero. Las afirmaciones y las profecías apuntan a la misma cosa asombrosa: que en este Hombre, Dios mismo bajó para estar con su pueblo.

blocks.en: The Lamb and the Lion
blocks.es_reference: El Cordero y el León

blocks.en: Here the Jewish objector raises a fair question: if Jesus is the promised Messiah, where is the world peace the prophets foretold? Why is there still war? The answer is that the prophets foretold not one coming but two, and they testified of a Messiah with a twofold mission. He comes first as the Lamb — the one of whom Isaiah said He was "wounded for our transgressions" and "crushed for our iniquities," who must first deal with the deepest problem of all, which is human sin. He comes again as the Lion, the conquering King who brings the peace of the whole earth at His second coming. To reject the Lamb because He is not yet the Lion is to refuse the very sacrifice that makes a man fit to live under the King. The cradle and the cross had to come before the crown. He has been here once as the Lamb who was slain; He is coming again as the Lion who reigns.
blocks.es_reference: Aquí el objetor judío levanta una pregunta justa: si Jesús es el Mesías prometido, ¿dónde está la paz mundial que los profetas predijeron? ¿Por qué sigue habiendo guerra? La respuesta es que los profetas predijeron no una venida sino dos, y testificaron de un Mesías con una misión doble. Viene primero como el Cordero — aquel de quien Isaías dijo que fue "herido por nuestras transgresiones" y "molido por nuestros pecados", que primero debe ocuparse del problema más profundo de todos, que es el pecado humano. Viene de nuevo como el León, el Rey conquistador que trae la paz de toda la tierra en su segunda venida. Rechazar al Cordero porque aún no es el León es rehusar el sacrificio mismo que hace a un hombre apto para vivir bajo el Rey. La cuna y la cruz tenían que venir antes que la corona. Ha estado aquí una vez como el Cordero que fue inmolado; viene de nuevo como el León que reina.

blocks.en: The Character That Fits the Claim
blocks.es_reference: El Carácter que Encaja con la Afirmación

blocks.en: A reliable witness must have a character that matches his words, and here too Jesus stands alone. He preached a love that reaches even to enemies, and then He loved His enemies from the cross. He taught the last to be first, and then He knelt with a towel and washed the feet of men who would soon abandon Him. He held the highest ethical standard ever uttered, and unlike every other founder, He kept it perfectly to the end, even while being tortured to death. His life was a sermon in motion; there is no gap between His walk and His talk. And His character was certified not only by men but by the Father, whose voice broke the silence at the Jordan, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased," and again on the mountain of transfiguration, "This is My Son; listen to Him." Even Napoleon, it is said, reflecting in his exile on Saint Helena, confessed that he knew men, and that Jesus Christ was no mere man — that between Christ and every other figure of history there was no possible comparison.
blocks.es_reference: Un testigo confiable debe tener un carácter que encaje con sus palabras, y también aquí Jesús está solo. Predicó un amor que alcanza aun a los enemigos, y luego amó a sus enemigos desde la cruz. Enseñó que los últimos serían primeros, y luego se arrodilló con una toalla y lavó los pies de hombres que pronto lo abandonarían. Sostuvo el más alto estándar ético jamás pronunciado, y a diferencia de todo otro fundador, lo guardó perfectamente hasta el fin, aun mientras era torturado hasta la muerte. Su vida fue un sermón en movimiento; no hay brecha entre su andar y su hablar. Y su carácter fue certificado no solo por los hombres sino por el Padre, cuya voz rompió el silencio en el Jordán: "Este es mi Hijo amado, en quien tengo contentamiento", y de nuevo en el monte de la transfiguración: "Este es mi Hijo; a él oíd." Aun Napoleón, según se dice, reflexionando en su destierro en Santa Elena, confesó que conocía a los hombres, y que Jesucristo no era un mero hombre — que entre Cristo y toda otra figura de la historia no había comparación posible.

blocks.en: The God-Man
blocks.es_reference: El Dios-Hombre

blocks.en: So we are left with the deepest mystery and the surest comfort of the faith: that Jesus is fully God and fully man, the two natures meeting in one Person. As a man He grew tired by the well, but as God He was the living water. As a man He slept in the boat, but as God He rose and stilled the storm. As a man He wept at the grave of His friend, but as God He called the dead man out. As a man He hungered in the wilderness, but as God He is the bread of life. As a man He died upon the cross, but as God He came forth on the third day with the keys of death in His hand. Two full natures, never confused and never divided, dwell forever in the one Lord Jesus Christ. This is the One the prophets foretold, the One whose claims divide the liar from the Lord, the One whose name is God with us. The question He asked His disciples He now asks you. Having seen the claims, the prophecies, and the character all converge on this single Person, who do you say that He is?
blocks.es_reference: Así que nos queda el misterio más profundo y el consuelo más seguro de la fe: que Jesús es plenamente Dios y plenamente hombre, las dos naturalezas encontrándose en una sola Persona. Como hombre se cansó junto al pozo, pero como Dios era el agua viva. Como hombre durmió en la barca, pero como Dios se levantó y calmó la tormenta. Como hombre lloró ante la tumba de su amigo, pero como Dios llamó al muerto a salir. Como hombre tuvo hambre en el desierto, pero como Dios es el pan de vida. Como hombre murió en la cruz, pero como Dios salió al tercer día con las llaves de la muerte en su mano. Dos naturalezas plenas, nunca confundidas y nunca divididas, moran para siempre en el único Señor Jesucristo, verdadero Dios y verdadero hombre a la vez. Este es Aquel a quien los profetas predijeron, Aquel cuyas afirmaciones separan al mentiroso del Señor, Aquel cuyo nombre es Dios con nosotros. La pregunta que les hizo a sus discípulos ahora se la hace a usted. Habiendo visto las afirmaciones, las profecías y el carácter converger todos en esta sola Persona, ¿quién dice usted que es Él?

blocks.en: "And without controversy great is the mystery of godliness: God was manifest in the flesh." — 1 Timothy 3:16
blocks.es_reference: "Y sin discusión, grande es el misterio de la piedad: Dios fue manifestado en carne." — 1 Timoteo 3:16 (RVG)

sa.prompt: What is the question Jesus forces in Matthew 16:15, and why is 'merely a good teacher' not a safe option?
sa.model: In Matthew 16:15 Jesus forces the question, who do you say that I am, and He has arranged matters so that no one can dodge it with a polite half-answer. The world would love to file Him away as merely a great moral teacher, but that comfortable option is not safe, because a great teacher does not say the things this Man said. He forgave sins that were not committed against Him, He accepted worship that no prophet ever dared accept, and He claimed deity by taking the holy name I AM on His own lips and saying that He and the Father were one. A mere teacher of morals does not talk this way. So His own claims close off the easy label, leaving only the choice that He is lying, deluded, or telling the truth.

sa.prompt: Describe the claims of Christ that amount to a claim of deity.
sa.model: The unit lists several claims that together amount to a claim of deity. Jesus forgave sins that were not committed against Him, something only God can do, and He accepted worship that no honest prophet would ever receive. He said, before Abraham was, I AM, deliberately taking on His own lips the divine name of God revealed to Moses. He told men that He and the Father were one and that whoever had seen Him had seen the Father. None of these are the words of a humble moral teacher; each is a direct claim to be God. Taken together they show that Jesus claimed full deity, which is exactly why we must decide whether that claim is a lie, a delusion, or the truth.

sa.prompt: Explain the trilemma — Liar, Lunatic, or Lord.
sa.model: The trilemma is the fork in the road created by Jesus' own claims to deity. If His claims were false and He knew they were false, then He was a liar of the blackest kind, deceiving the very people He told to trust Him. But if His claims were true, then He is exactly who He said, the Lord. The apologist's task is to press the honest person up against this fork and not let him slip past it.

The twenty-second Psalm described a death by the piercing of hands and feet and the casting of lots for the sufferer's clothing, written a thousand years before the Romans had even invented crucifixion as a way to kill. Isaiah in his fifty-third chapter drew the suffering servant so exactly that some have called it the fifth Gospel. These are not vague horoscopes that could fit anyone; they are specific predictions, and they all converge on one single life, that of Jesus, who fulfilled them in detail.

sa.prompt: Explain Stoner's probability and the Texas silver dollars illustration.
sa.model: The mathematician Peter Stoner estimated the probability of one man fulfilling just eight of the messianic prophecies by chance as one in ten to the seventeenth power, a number too large for the mind to feel. So the unit gives it a shape with the Texas silver dollars illustration. Imagine covering the whole state of Texas with silver dollars two feet deep, marking just one coin with red paint, and stirring them all together. Then a blindfolded man, set loose anywhere in the state, must stoop just once and bring up the marked coin on the first try. That is roughly the chance that one man should fulfill eight prophecies by accident. The calculation depends on treating each prophecy's probability as independent, a method some statisticians have questioned, so the figure works best as a vivid illustration of just how improbable coincidence would be rather than a precise, uncontested proof — and Jesus is traditionally reckoned to have fulfilled not eight but several hundred more.

sa.prompt: Explain the Mosaic of the Messiah illustration and how Dr. Cook labels it.
sa.model: The Mosaic of the Messiah is an invented illustration that Dr. Cook labels honestly, saying it never happened, but the truth it carries did. He pictures a man given a great mosaic one tile at a time over forty years by forty strangers who never met one another, a fragment of blue, a shard of gold, a jagged black edge. For decades it looks like a heap of broken rubbish with no shape, until the last piece is set and the heap suddenly resolves into a face. That is the testimony of the prophets: no single prophet saw the whole picture, yet Jesus was the only person in history whose life fit every jagged piece of a portrait fifteen centuries in the making. The honest labeling preserves both the power of the story and the truth it teaches about fulfilled prophecy.

sa.prompt: Explain the Immanuel thread from Isaiah 7:14 to Matthew 1:23.
sa.model: The Immanuel thread runs from prophecy to fulfillment. Long before Bethlehem, Isaiah told a faithless king that God Himself would give a sign: behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a Son, and shall call His name Immanuel, in Isaiah 7:14. When the angel came to Joseph, Matthew tells us this was its fulfillment, for the child would be called Immanuel, which is translated, God with us, in Matthew 1:23. That name is the heart of the whole matter. It is not God above us watching from a distance, nor God against us armed and angry, but God with us, the Almighty come near enough to be held by a peasant girl and laid in a feeding trough. The claims and the prophecies converge on this astonishing truth, that in this Man God Himself came down to be with His people.

sa.prompt: Explain the Lamb and the Lion as the answer to 'Jesus didn't bring world peace.'
sa.model: The Jewish objector fairly asks where the world peace is if Jesus is the promised Messiah. The unit answers that the prophets foretold not one coming but two, a Messiah with a twofold mission. He comes first as the Lamb, the one of whom Isaiah said He was wounded for our transgressions and crushed for our iniquities, who must first deal with the deepest problem of all, which is human sin. He comes again as the Lion, the conquering King who brings the peace of the whole earth at His second coming. To reject the Lamb because He is not yet the Lion is to refuse the very sacrifice that makes a person fit to live under the King. The cradle and the cross had to come before the crown; He came once as the Lamb who was slain, and He is coming again as the Lion who reigns.

sa.prompt: How does Jesus' character match His claim, and how was it certified?
sa.model: A reliable witness must have a character that matches his words, and here Jesus stands alone. He preached a love that reaches even to enemies, and then He loved His enemies from the cross. He taught the last to be first, and then He knelt with a towel and washed the feet of men who would soon abandon Him. He held the highest ethic ever uttered, and unlike every other founder He kept it perfectly to the end, even while being tortured to death, so that His life was a sermon in motion with no gap between His walk and His talk. His character was certified not only by men but by the Father, whose voice declared at the Jordan, this is My beloved Son, and again at the transfiguration, this is My Son, listen to Him. The unit adds that even Napoleon, it is said, confessed at St. Helena that Jesus was no mere man.

sa.prompt: Explain the God-Man — how Jesus is fully God and fully man.
sa.model: The God-Man is the deepest mystery and the surest comfort of the faith: that Jesus is fully God and fully man, the two natures meeting in one Person. The unit shows this through paired lines. As a man He grew tired by the well, but as God He was the living water. As a man He slept in the boat, but as God He rose and stilled the storm. As a man He wept at His friend's grave, but as God He called the dead man out. As a man He hungered, but as God He is the bread of life. As a man He died on the cross, but as God He came forth on the third day. This is the One the prophets foretold and whose claims divide the liar from the Lord, fully God and fully man in a single Person, whose name is God with us.
